items.heading: The Instinct Most Freshers Follow
items.text: The instinct most freshers follow is to structure the resume the way a textbook resume template looks: objective, education, skills, then whatever is left. That order buries your strongest material under the least useful part of the page.

items.heading: Here Is a Practical Section
items.text: Here is a practical section order that puts your strongest evidence in the first screen a recruiter or ATS parser sees.

visuals.title: Key ideas behind The Instinct Most Freshers Follow

visuals.heading: The Section Order That Actually Works

rows: Name, phone, email, city, LinkedIn URL, and a portfolio/GitHub link if relevant. No photo, no age, no marital status.
Degree, strongest skill area, and one specific thing you have built or done. Written for the exact role, not copy-pasted across applications.
Grouped by type (languages, tools, frameworks, soft skills) in a plain comma-separated line, not a graphic skill bar.
Your strongest 2-4 projects, each with the problem, what you built, tools used, and one measurable outcome.

items.heading: Move Skills and Projects Above
items.text: Move skills and projects above education. Education is a credential; projects and skills are evidence.

items.heading: Use Coursework and Extracurriculars Only
items.text: Use coursework and extracurriculars only when they support a specific claim, not as filler to make the page look fuller.
